    Paths with all consecutive pairs occurring (Step 2 of Proposition 3.8) #

    For a brick string module over a special biserial algebra, a path occurs on the string diagram as soon as each of its arrows and each pair of consecutive arrows does (seg_of_chain), by induction with seg_of_overlap.

    L ≠ [] → (∀ x ∈ L, ∃ (d : Bool) (r : ℕ), w.Seg d r [x]) → List.IsChain (fun (x y : D.Q.A) => ∃ (d : Bool) (r : ℕ), w.Seg d r [x, y]) L → ∃ (d : Bool) (r : ℕ), w.Seg d r L

    A path occurs once its arrows and consecutive pairs occur.
